description.narrative: The objective of the Project is to increase economic inclusion of under-employed and under-educated youth aged 15-30 and strengthen employment services and the technical and vocational training system.

The proposed project will support the Government of Benin's efforts to create more, better, and inclusive jobs by supporting Azoli, an active labor market program designed to strengthen labor supply, stimulate labor demand, and improve information and intermediation for vulnerable youth. It aims to reinforce employment services and vocational training to provide vulnerable youth with skills aligned to market demand, as well as to improve their access to financial services. The project pays special attention to women, youth living in violence-prone areas and persons with disabilities.

condition.narrative: Schedule 2, Section I.A.2.a: The Recipient shall establish within three (3) months after the Effective Date and maintain throughoutProject implementation, a project steering committee with composition, mandate and resources satisfactory to the Association.

Schedule 2, Section I.A.3.c: The Recipient shall, within six (6) months after the Effective Date or any later date as may be agreedwith the Association, recruit, and thereafter maintain during the implementation of the Project, an independent external auditorfor the Project, with qualifications, experience and under terms of reference acceptable to the Association.

Schedule 2, Section I.A.4.a: The Recipient shall establish within three (3) months after the Effective Date and thereafter maintainthroughout Project implementation, a technical committee for the Project, with a composition, mandate and resources satisfactory tothe Association.

Schedule 2, Section I.A.5.a: The Recipient shall establish within three (3) months after the Effective Date, and thereaftermaintain throughout Project implementation, a management committee responsible for Part 2 of the Project, with a composition,mandate and resources satisfactory to the Association.

Schedule 2, Section IV.A.1.a (i): The Recipient shall within three (3) months after the Effective Date recruit for FODEFCA: (A) anaccountant who shall report directly to the PCss financial management specialist; and (B) a procurement specialist who shallreportdirectly to the Project coordinator, all responsible for Part 2 of the Project, and with qualifications, experience andreferences acceptable to the Association, and all in accordance with this Agreement and the PIM.

Schedule 2, Section IV.A.1.a (ii): The Recipient shall within three (3) months after the Effective Date recruit for ANPE: (A) anaccountant for Part 1 and 3 of the Project who shall report directly to the PCss financial management specialist; and (B) aprocurement specialist for Parts 1, 3 and 4 of the Project who shall report directly to the Project coordinator, all withqualifications, experience and references acceptable to the Association, and all in accordance with this Agreement and the PIM.

Schedule 2, Section IV.A.1.a (iii): The Recipient shall within three (3) months after the Effective Date install an accountingsystem within FODEFCA, ANPE and the PCS, in form and substance satisfactory to the Association.

Schedule 2, Section IV.A.1.b : The Recipient shall within six (6) months after the Effective Date, enter into an agreement with theGeneral Inspectorate of Finance for the purpose of including the Project in its annual work program and conducting semi-annualinternal audits of the Project, and causing the General Inspectorate of Finance to submit semi-annual internal audit reports to theAssociation within forty-five (45) days after the end of the audit period.

Schedule 2, Section IV.B.a: The Recipient shall, through the MPMEPE ensure that, within six (6) months after the Effective Date,each commune within the Recipient's territory has: (i) set up a Local Employment Promotion Unit (“ULPE”) with a composition,mandate and resources satisfactory to the Association, including at least one communal agent with qualifications and experiencesatisfactory to the Association; or (ii) put in place alternative measures in the event of the unavailability of qualified stafffor the ULPE at the commune level, all in a manner satisfactory to the Association.

title.narrative: Youth satisfied with the Azôli program

comment.narrative: 87.7 percent of program recipients reported satisfaction with the services they benefited from, according to the results of the Iterative Beneficiary Monitoring (IBM) survey conducted in September 2024.

title.narrative: Youth completing the Azôli program who reside in areas at risk of violent extremism

comment.narrative: Data reported on the monitoring platform puts this rate at 24 percent.

title.narrative: The MIS for the management of the Azôli program is developed and operational

comment.narrative: The MIS has been fully operational since late June 2023.

title.narrative: Youth completing small business training under the project

comment.narrative: 21,024 beneficiaries have completed the small business training.

title.narrative: Beneficiaries of social safety net programs

comment.narrative: These are the beneficiaries of the apprenticeship support program pilot targeting 600 young girls coming from extreme poor households or areas at risk of extreme violence. There are 401 beneficiaries so far.

The Project supports the CQP training for 3,832 candidates in 17 trades. It is expected that at least 3,000 of them will get their certification by December 2025. In addition, 1,000 youths will be supported to enter poultry value chains and get their certification by June 2027.

title.narrative: Curricula developed for identified trades, including renewed curricula

comment.narrative: 17 curricula have been developed or renewed under the Project.

title.narrative: At least one CFP per trade has the necessary equipment and human resources to offer training in the supported trades for the CQP

comment.narrative: The implementing agencies (FODEFCA and DESTFP) have identified the reference training centers for the 10 trades selected. Procurement of equipment for these centers is underway and has been completed for 2 trades thus far.

title.narrative: The MIS for the management of the technical training and the apprenticeship system is developed and operational

comment.narrative: The MIS for the management of the technical training and the apprenticeship system has been developed. It is expected to be fully operational by Q2 2026.

title.narrative: Female youth registered in the CQP training out of the total number of registered apprentices supported by the project

comment.narrative: There are only 1,423 girls among the 5,124 candidates who started the CQP training, representing 27.8 percent. Efforts made with the support of NGOs specializing in gender issues to ensure better representation of girls helped raise the ratio of girls from 12.40 percent to 27.8 percent between the first and second cohorts but have not led to the 50 percent ratio being achieved.
According to the latest survey conducted by local employment agents, 70.13 percent of beneficiaries indicated that their income had increased after their participation in the program.

title.narrative: Youth benefiting from Business Development Services

comment.narrative: 1,014 startup/young entrepreneurs have benefited from the Business Development Services.

title.narrative: Youth benefiting from business development services accessing financial services to expand their business

comment.narrative: This activity is scheduled for Q1-2026.

title.narrative: Youth supported by the project receiving the Certificat de Qualification Professionnelle (CQP)

comment.narrative: 1,802 candidates passed the CQP exam in March 2025.

title.narrative: Youth receiving the Certificat de Qualification au MEtier (CQM) in trades supported by the project

comment.narrative: 12,183 have already received the Certificat de Qualification au MEtier (CQM) in trades supported by the Project.
So far, 20,157 recipients have benefited from short-term technical training.

title.narrative: Master artisans receiving technical and pedagogical training and/or business development services

comment.narrative: Of the 904 master craftsmen enrolled, 809 have completed training in the first 10 trades.

title.narrative: The dropout rates of CQP apprentices supported by the Project [Percentage point]

comment.narrative: Estimated from the first cohort of beneficiaries.

title.narrative: Young women coming from very poor households or areas at risk of violent extremism supported for apprenticeship

comment.narrative: 401 young women coming from very poor households are currently benefiting from the apprenticeship program that started in Q1 2024.

To date, 18,784 beneficiaries have been assisted by the National Microfinance Fund under the Project to open savings accounts and use them for their business (under Component 1) or to cover training costs (under Component 2).

title.narrative: Youth receiving cash grants under the project

comment.narrative: 18,784 recipients have benefited from the start-up grant.

title.narrative: Municipalities where the Azôli program is operational

comment.narrative: The Azôli program is fully operational in all Benin 77 communes.

title.narrative: Youth in apprenticeship satisfied with the training received in the Vocational Training Center

comment.narrative: 94.6 percent of program recipients reported satisfaction with the training received in the Vocational Training Centers, according to the results of the Iterative Beneficiary Monitoring (IBM) survey conducted in September 2024.

title.narrative: The delivery mechanisms and processes of the Azôli program are adapted to integrate key learning and beneficiary feedback before the enrolment of new beneficiary cohorts (Yes/No)

comment.narrative: Key learnings from the evaluations conducted so far (IBM surveys, process evaluations conducted in November 2022 and September 2024, and qualitative studies conducted in October 2023 under a PEI grant) have been reflected in the delivery process.
By October 27, 2025, 258,451 young applicants registered for the Azôli program using the SIC@2 platform.

title.narrative: Beneficiaries following the wage employment pathways

comment.narrative: As of September 30, 2025, 29,017 beneficiaries have started or completed their internship.

title.narrative: Youth completing life skills training under the project

comment.narrative: So far, 54,200 beneficiaries have completed the life skills training.

title.narrative: Direct project beneficiaries who were underemployed, and/or with low level of education, at the beginning of training

comment.narrative: According to the results of the second follow-up survey carried out in September 2024, all the beneficiaries were underemployed but only 74.36 percent of them had little or no education (maximum junior high school level) before entering the program. Many youths with higher school level are keen to join the Azôli program, as there is not yet a program for them. What's more, their profile is also in demand by some companies. To take this into account, the target for this indicator has been lowered from 95% to 80% following the mid-term review, given that most of the youths concerned are actually underemployed, even if they have a level of education higher than junior high school.

title.narrative: The list of areas at risk of violent extremism as well as the positive discrimination strategy towards these areas are adopted by the Steering Committee

comment.narrative: The list of areas at risk of violent extremism was developed by the ABeGIEF (Beninese integrated border management Agency) and the CNL-CREVT (National Commission for Countering Radicalization, Violent Extremism and Terrorism) and adopted by the Steering Committee in Q4-2021.

title.narrative: People benefiting from actions to increase access to more and better jobs to advance gender equality

comment.narrative: To date, 23,777 young women have benefited from the project's interventions, which include Azôli, Business Development Services (BDS), Technical and Vocational Education and Training (TVET), and apprenticeship support.
As of now, 29,017 beneficiaries of the Azôli internship program have received monthly stipends via mobile money services or bank accounts.

title.narrative: The CQP certification processes are organized for renewed or new identified trades

comment.narrative: The curricula have been renewed or newly developed for 17 trades supported by the project. The CQP test was organized in March 2025 in 10 of these 17 trades. A second test is set in November 2025 in the 7 remaining trades.

title.narrative: Beneficiaries in employment (whether salaried or self-employed) 12 months after support

comment.narrative: Results from the latest IBM survey completed in September 2024.

title.narrative: ANPE adopts the tools and services developed under the Azôli program as key processes of its delivery system

comment.narrative: All Azôli-related tools are developed by AnpE (with the support of project staff and technical assistance from the World Bank). As a result, the AnpE has already adopted most of the tools developed under Azôli as part of its delivery system. An evaluation will be conducted at the end of the Project to confirm this.

title.narrative: The gender gap in underemployed status of beneficiaries of the Azôli program (who worked less than 40 hours over the last 7 days, not by choice)

target.value: Less than half of the gap at entry (2.08)

comment.narrative: The gender gap is currently estimated at 0.6 compared to the 4.16 initial gap.
